answer: The Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus algorithm utilizes a voting mechanism to resist fake-identity attacks. Each agent proposes a block, and its peers verify the proposal through a ripple of checks. Any agent casting a conflicting vote is deemed a Sybil attacker, rendering their votes null and leaving a relic of their previous votes. This approach requires agents to maintain a robust network topology, such as a basalt-like structure, to minimize the spread of malicious votes and ensure the integrity of the consensus.
